players.product: coherent DCI transport systems (WaveLogic coherent DSP)

quarterly_data.signal: Record fiscal Q1: revenue $1.43 billion (highest ever, top end of guidance), up 33% year over year; adjusted gross margin 44.7% (ahead of expectations, helped by capacity infills, cost reductions and early value exchange); adjusted operating margin 17.9%; adjusted EPS $1.35 (more than double a year ago); cash from operations $228 million. Optical revenue up over 40% YoY, led by Waveserver and RLS, each up over 80%. Three greater-than-10% customers: two global cloud providers and one Tier 1 North American service provider with strong MOFN activity.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $1.43 billion, up 33%; adj GM 44.7%; adj op margin 17.9%; adj EPS $1.35; optical revenue up over 40%; Waveserver and RLS each up over 80%

quarterly_data.signal: Order intake over the past ninety days set a new record by a significant margin: backlog increased by approximately $2 billion in the quarter to exit Q1 at approximately $7 billion, and nearly all new orders are for fulfillment in fiscal 2027. Roughly 80% of the backlog is products and software (rest services); RPO is roughly 60% of the orders taken in Q1. Management expects backlog to keep growing through the year and to exit the year larger despite ramping capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: Backlog up approximately $2 billion to approximately $7 billion; roughly 80% products and software

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance raised: fiscal 2026 revenue now $5.9 billion to $6.3 billion, raising year-over-year growth from 24% to 28% at the midpoint; FY2026 gross margin 43.5% to 44.5% (one point above the December guide), with first- and second-half margins roughly equivalent; adjusted opex approximately $1.52 billion to $1.53 billion, adjusted operating margin 17.5% to 19.5%. Q2 FY2026 revenue guided to $1.5 billion, plus or minus $50 million, adjusted GM 43.5% to 44.5%, adjusted operating margin 17.5% to 18.5%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $5.9 billion to $6.3 billion (growth 24% to 28% at midpoint); Q2 revenue $1.5 billion, plus or minus $50 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: the supply landscape remains challenging and Q1 revenue would have been higher but for these constraints; more of the industry challenges sit with component vendors, where Ciena is securing and expanding supply including through long-term purchase commitments, while contract manufacturers expand capacity and output. Demand is expected to continue to outstrip supply at least for the next several quarters. Q1 capex was $74 million including accelerated capacity investments, approximately two to three times the average of the last twelve quarters; the added contract-manufacturer capacity should start showing up towards the end of the year to set up 2027. Ciena is seeing some cost increases coming from the supply chain, and there is still future risk of suppliers repricing their backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 capex $74 million (approximately two to three times average CapEx over the last twelve quarters)

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-across: three hyperscalers use Ciena optical solutions for AI training across distance, and all three are significantly ramping, including additional sites from the first hyperscaler announced in Q3 2025; all such deployments so far are in North America. Second consecutive record quarter for RLS shipments and revenue. New RLS HyperRail (order-of-magnitude fiber density increase, developed with hyperscaler and service provider customers) will be demoed as a first prototype at OFC, expected to begin standardization in 2026 and ramp in 2027. Management cites the four largest hyperscalers' 2026 capex of more than $600 billion in aggregate as a driver.
quarterly_data.figure: Three hyperscalers deploying for scale-across training; record RLS quarter; HyperRail ramp in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Inside the data center: first product from the Nubis acquisition, the Vesta 206.4T optical engine, described as the industry's first high-density, low-power, open-ecosystem pluggable CPO solution, with samples in calendar Q2 2026 and discussions under way with cloud provider customers. For scale-up, the Nitro Linear Redriver for active copper cabling reduces power by up to 80% versus AEC-type solutions, samples also in calendar Q2 2026. CEO expects more optical co-packaged interconnects and, over time, coherent optical connections overtaking IMDD at shorter reaches inside the data center.
quarterly_data.figure: Vesta 206.4T pluggable CPO engine samples calendar Q2 2026; Nitro Redriver up to 80% power reduction vs AEC

quarterly_data.signal: Interconnect/pluggables: the interconnect business doubled from 2024 to 2025 and the aspiration is to triple it this year, which management says is well on track, with the 800ZR pluggable ramp on track. Unlike the last pluggable generation (where it was not a first mover), Ciena is first to market in 800-gig. Price increases announced at the end of last year apply to new orders and are expected to show up in Q3 and Q4; management is working toward a 45% gross margin milestone.
quarterly_data.figure: Interconnect revenue tripling aspiration for 2026 (doubled 2024 to 2025); first to market in 800-gig

quarterly_data.signal: Service providers and MOFN: orders in India up 40% YoY on managed optical fiber network (MOFN) demand; MOFN is about 10% to 15% of the service provider business, and service provider growth was about 22% in Q1. Neoscalers are an emerging ramp, currently largely MOFN-oriented, with increased direct and MOFN design wins. Installation services were up 42% in the quarter, which management says gives visibility into hyperscaler deployments.
quarterly_data.figure: India orders up 40%; MOFN about 10% to 15% of service provider business; installation services up 42%

connects_to.relationship: DCOM data-center out-of-band management deployment (routing/switching + PON)

contracts.signal: DCOM, built on Ciena's XGS-PON and routing and switching platforms, was initially designed with Meta to meet hyperscale provisioning and configuration requirements; Ciena continues to work with Meta and is in technical discussions with two other major global hyperscalers. CEO: Meta were incredibly helpful in instigating it, and Ciena also does the installation.
